Thank you for using myRSync.

 myRSync is an Android rsync client for backing up and syncing folders to a server you control — over SSH (key or password) or an rsync daemon.

 Free to try: one configuration with manual runs. Unlock Pro (one-time) for unlimited configs, schedules, and Tasker / Locale. No ads.

 Open source (GPLv3): https://github.com/socratesx/myrsync
 Bundled rsync 3.4.1 — https://rsync.samba.org

 Contact / bugs: myrsync@protonmail.com
 Tips (optional): https://paypal.me/myrsync

 Disclaimer: You are solely responsible for your configurations and options. Wrong paths, push/pull direction, or delete options can permanently overwrite or remove data. Prefer a dry run (-n) first if you are unsure. The author is not liable for data loss.

myRSync runs rsync using the servers, paths, and options you configure.

Incorrect settings can permanently delete, overwrite, or move files on this device or on remote servers.

By tapping Accept, you agree that:

• You alone are responsible for your configurations and for verifying them (for example with a dry run) before relying on them.
• The developer is not liable for any data loss or damage from use or misuse of this app.

If you do not accept these terms, the app will close.

myRSync builds and runs rsync jobs on your phone — sync with a remote host over SSH or an rsync daemon, on demand or on a schedule.

 Ideal for NAS / VPS / homelab backups under your control (not a proprietary cloud).

 How to use:

 1. Create a configuration (Transport: SSH or Rsync Daemon; Push or Pull).
 2. For SSH: set host, user, remote path, and a private key or password. Default port is 22 if left blank.
 3. For Daemon: set host, user, module, and port (default 873).
 4. Choose the local path and rsync options (use -n dry-run to test safely).
 5. Save, then Run Now from Configurations — or add schedules (Pro).
 6. Check Overview for next/last run status and Log for rsync output.
 7. Optional (Pro): fire a saved config from Tasker / Locale.

 Free: one config, manual runs. Pro unlocks unlimited configs, schedules, and Tasker.

 Grant All files access (and Alarms & reminders for schedules) when prompted so jobs can reach your folders and run on time.

-v, increase verbosity 
	 -q, suppress non-error messages 
	 -a, archive mode; equals -rlptgoD 
	 -z, compress file data during the transfer 
	 -r, recurse into directories 
	 -u, skip files that are newer on the receiver 
	 -p, preserve permissions 
	 -o, preserve owner (super-user only) 
	 -g, preserve group 
	 -t, preserve modification times 
	 -n, perform a trial run with no changes made (dry run) 
	 -m, prune empty directory chains from file-list 
	 -O, omit directories from —times

Use this form to build an rsync job. Pick a transport first:

 • SSH — connect with a private key or password (default port 22). Remote Path is the path on the server (for example /home/user/backup).
 • Rsync Daemon — connect to rsyncd (default port 873). Module is the name from rsyncd.conf.

 Daemon setup docs: https://download.samba.org/pub/rsync/rsyncd.conf.html

 Command shapes:

 Push (SSH):
 rsync [OPTIONS] LOCAL_PATH user@host:REMOTE_PATH

 Pull (SSH):
 rsync [OPTIONS] user@host:REMOTE_PATH LOCAL_PATH

 Push (Daemon):
 rsync [OPTIONS] LOCAL_PATH rsync://[USER@]HOST[:PORT]/MODULE

 Pull (Daemon):
 rsync [OPTIONS] rsync://[USER@]HOST[:PORT]/MODULE LOCAL_PATH

 How to fill the form:

 1. Choose SSH or Rsync Daemon, and Push or Pull.
 2. Enter host / IP. Leave port blank for defaults (22 / 873).
 3. Enter username. For daemon, use the user allowed on that module; for SSH, the shell account.
 4. Daemon: enter the module name. SSH: enter remote path and key or password.
 5. Select the local path (Add Path or type it).
 6. Tick options (see ?). Use -n for a dry run before real syncs.
 7. Optionally add schedules (Pro), then View Command to preview paths/options.
 8. Save. Run from Configurations, Overview, or Tasker (Pro).

Schedules are attached to a configuration (Pro).

 1. Open a configuration and use the Schedules section.
 2. Add one or more schedules: time, weekdays, and optional Wi‑Fi-only.
 3. Each schedule needs at least one weekday.
 4. Save the configuration. Overview shows next/last run.

 Note: Android battery optimizations can delay alarms by a few minutes. Allow Alarms & reminders when prompted for more reliable timing.

The folder you selected is not writable by this application 

 This is due to Android's security policy and permission enforcement on the External SD Directories. 

 The Android allows writing to specific folders such as the /storage/emulated/0/. You can create a subfolder there and use it with rsync pull. If you want to save to a folder of your choice, anywhere on internal or external SD then root access is required. 

 If your device is rooted you can enable the root access feature from the settings and then you can select any existing path.

You can add options manually by using this textbox. 

 Any options string you add here will be added as it is and after any selected checkbox options.

 You are completely responsible for the correct syntax of the options string of the rsync command. 

 The app cannot validate that the options string is correct. Use the view command button to see the path/option preview.

 Flags that duplicate a checked option above (for example -n / --dry-run when -n is checked) are ignored.

 This is a potentially dangerous feature that may result in data loss. Take caution when using options that delete files.
How myRSync handles data on your device
myRSync needs All files access so scheduled and manual rsync jobs can read and write the folders you configure. On the next screen, enable access for this app.

myRSync needs access to your local network so it can sync with a computer on your Wi-Fi, such as a NAS or home server. Without this, those connections time out. A public internet address does not need it. Scheduled and Tasker runs use the choice you make here.
Local network access is turned off for myRSync. Syncs to a computer on your Wi-Fi will time out until you allow Nearby devices for this app. On the next screen, open Permissions and allow it.
